chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughter when there are no daughters of the deceased and no other heir besides them; and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son when there are no daughters or sons of the deceased and no other heir besides them.

key_terms.بَنَاتُ الِابْنَةِ: Daughters of the daughter (granddaughters via daughter)
key_terms.بَنَاتُ الِابْنِ: Daughters of the son (granddaughters via son)
key_terms.يَقُمْنَ مَقَامَ: Stand in the place of / represent

ai.seo_question: How do granddaughters inherit in Shia Islamic law when there are no direct children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'ta'sib' (residuary inheritance) for grandchildren, establishing that granddaughters through a daughter inherit as daughters in the absence of other female heirs, while granddaughters through a son inherit as sons when there are no direct children. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to ensuring equitable distribution among descendants by treating grandchildren as primary heirs when their parent is deceased or excluded, a nuance often discussed in contrast to Sunni schools regarding the 'hajb' (blocking) of grandchildren by sons. The text underscores the flexibility of Shia inheritance law in adapting to specific family structures to prevent the exclusion of close descendants.
